outcome: Still open in every source I could read: no ZFC construction of a Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω and no ZFC proof that none exists. The in-window items touching ℵ_ω are a revised version of a conditional result (Ben-Neria and Lücke, v2 18 Apr 2024, first posted Mar 2023) and an AI-assisted forum claim about a different problem (Erdős #623, June 2026) that does not bear on this question.
problem_asks: One existence question: is there an algebra A with |A| = ℵ_ω and no proper subalgebra of cardinality ℵ_ω? Parts: (1) the object, an algebra of size exactly ℵ_ω (Wikipedia's Jónsson cardinal article defines it as an algebra with no proper subalgebras of the same cardinality; 'algebra' there means a model of a language with countably many function symbols); (2) the two answers: a yes needs such an A; a no is equivalent to ℵ_ω being a Jónsson cardinal (every algebra of size ℵ_ω has a proper subalgebra of size ℵ_ω). The statement names no extra hypothesis, so it is read as a question in ZFC. Terminology trap: 'ℵ_ω is Jónsson' is the negative answer, and the Jónsson-cardinal literature (Eskew, Dimonte, Ben-Neria and Lücke) states results on that side.

events.what_happened: Omer Ben-Neria and Philipp Lücke, 'On Σ1-definable closed unbounded sets' (arXiv:2303.08251). Section 4.3 opens by saying the work is 'motivated by the notoriously open question whether the first limit cardinal ℵ_ω can be Jónsson'. Theorem 4.14: if ℵ_ω is Jónsson, then every infinite subset of {ℵ_n : n<ω} is Σ1-stationary in ℵ_ω, and every Σ1-definable regressive function on ℵ_ω (parameters in H(ℵ_ω) ∪ {ℵ_ω}) is constant on an infinite subset of {ℵ_n}. Theorem 5.3 (§5.2): equiconsistency over ZFC of a measurable cardinal with 'every unbounded subset of {ℵ_n} is Σ1(Ord)-stationary in ℵ_ω' (a different property from Jónssonness). Section 6 lists Questions 6.1, 6.3 (assuming ℵ_ω Jónsson) and 6.4; none asks existence. Journal status (Canadian Journal of Mathematics, accepted/in press 2025, online 14 Jan 2025) is from search snippets, not opened.
events.revisions: v1 14 Mar 2023 (33 KB); v2 18 Apr 2024, 'revised version, 32 pages', no changelog shown. Journal version accepted/online 2025 per search snippet (not opened).
events.delivers: Conditional only: assuming ℵ_ω is Jónsson (i.e. no Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω), the Σ1-stationarity and regressive-function consequences of Theorem 4.14 follow. Theorem 5.3 is an unconditional consistency-strength statement about the different property of Σ1(Ord)-stationarity of {ℵ_n} at ℵ_ω. Neither establishes existence or non-existence of a Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω in ZFC. The stated aim (talk abstracts, not the paper) is to restrict the models of set theory in which ℵ_ω is Jónsson.
events.remains: Whether ℵ_ω is Jónsson in ZFC, i.e. whether a Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω exists, and whether ℵ_ω can be Jónsson relative to large cardinals. The paper's Question 6.3 is posed under the Jónsson assumption, so it does not address the existence question.

events.what_happened: Monroe Eskew, 'On a strengthening of Jónssonness for ℵ_ω' (arXiv:1910.05834). Studies a family of strengthenings of 'ℵ_ω is Jónsson' indexed by reals and identifies the strongest, s1-Jónsson. Proves Silver's theorem (Theorem 4): if ℵ_ω is Jónsson and 2^ℵ0 < ℵ_ω, then ℵ_ω is f-Jónsson for some increasing f ≠ id. Theorem 7: s1-Jónsson implies f-Jónsson for every increasing f with f(0)=0. Shows a barrier to weakening Silver's hypothesis. States that the consistency of ℵ_ω being Jónsson relative to large cardinals is open.
events.delivers: Only conditional statements: each result assumes ℵ_ω is Jónsson (or f-Jónsson) and derives consequences of that assumption. No unconditional existence or non-existence claim. Silver's theorem is a sufficient condition for a consequence of the no-algebra side, not a resolution.
events.remains: Whether ℵ_ω is Jónsson in ZFC; whether it is consistent relative to large cardinals (the paper says this is open).

events.direction: Conditional, on the 'no Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω' side: every result assumes ℵ_ω is Jónsson.

events.what_happened: Vincenzo Dimonte, 'Generic I0 at ℵ_ω' (arXiv:1609.07970). Introduces a generic large cardinal akin to I0. Abstract: when ℵ_ω is such a cardinal, 'ℵ_ω is Jónsson'; in a choiceless inner model many properties hold that contrast with PCF theory in ZFC. Forcing and inner model details are not in the abstract page read. Talk at KGRC, 19 Mar 2015 (search snippet).
events.revisions: v1 26 Sep 2016; v2 22 Sep 2017; v3 18 Dec 2017 (current).
events.delivers: Conditional: under a generic I0-type hypothesis at ℵ_ω (witnessed by a forcing, in the paper's sense), ℵ_ω is Jónsson, i.e. no Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω. The setting is choiceless; the result is not a ZFC theorem and does not decide the ZFC question. Restricted to the hypothesis.
events.remains: The ZFC question. The consistency of the generic I0 hypothesis is not established in the sources read.
events.time_since_posted: About 10 years since v1; no journal version or public verification found in searches (not exhaustive)
events.doubts: Only the abstract page was read, not the paper. The abstract states the result in a choiceless inner model, and whether the hypothesis is consistent is not stated in what I read.
events.direction: Conditional on the 'no Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω' side under a hypothesis that is not ZFC.

events.what_happened: Saharon Shelah, 'Jonsson algebras in successor cardinals' (Israel J. Math. 30 (1978), 57–64): a Jónsson algebra on ℵ_{ω+1}, using pcf theory (first introduced in this paper, per search snippet). Rinot's survey bibliography (fetched) also cites Shelah, 'ℵ_{ω+1} has a Jonsson algebra', in Cardinal Arithmetic (1994). Reported hypothesis in secondary sources: 2^ℵ0 ≤ ℵ_{ω+1}. Neither primary paper was opened.
events.delivers: Neighbouring result: a Jónsson algebra on ℵ_{ω+1}, the successor of ℵ_ω. With the successor transfer (if κ is not Jónsson then κ+ is not Jónsson, per Eskew's notes via search snippet), this makes ℵ_ω the least cardinal where the question is open. It does not decide the ℵ_ω case.

Abstract (opened page): Jónsson algebras on many inaccessibles, including the first regular Jónsson cardinal that is λ×ω-Mahlo; further restrictions on successors of singular Jónsson cardinals; a Jónsson algebra on the successor of beth_ω. The abstract never mentions ℵ_ω.

events.what_happened: Jordan DuBeau, 'Jónsson Jónsson-Tarski algebras' (arXiv:2202.02460, first submitted 5 Feb 2022; v2 10 Sep 2022). Abstract: in the variety of Jónsson-Tarski algebras, Jónsson algebras cannot have cardinality greater than ℵ_1, and 2^ℵ1 pairwise nonisomorphic ones exist. Also a result for residually small varieties with cf(|J|) > 2^{|L|+}. Journal (Algebra Universalis) per search snippet, not verified.
events.delivers: Restricted to specific varieties (Jónsson-Tarski, residually small with a cofinality condition). Within the Jónsson-Tarski variety, every Jónsson algebra has cardinality at most ℵ_1. Nothing about ℵ_ω in the usual, unrestricted sense.
events.remains: The question for arbitrary algebras of size ℵ_ω.
events.time_since_posted: About 4 years 8 months since v1; journal status not verified
events.direction: Analogue question (variety-restricted). Cuts toward no Jónsson algebras above ℵ_1 in that variety only.
events.object: Constructs 2^ℵ1 pairwise nonisomorphic Jónsson algebras of size ℵ_1 in the Jónsson-Tarski variety. The abstract does not describe them further.

events.what_happened: Assaf Rinot, 'May the successor of a singular cardinal be Jónsson?' (arXiv:2312.08253). A survey collecting necessary conditions for the successor of a singular cardinal to be Jónsson. The arXiv text (opened) does not mention ℵ_ω at all; the only ℵ_{ω+1} mention is a bibliography entry. Its introduction says it 'centers around the open problem of whether the successor of a singular cardinal may consistently be Jónsson'. The author's blog (opened) says it was updated Nov 2025 and accepted by Bollettino dell'Unione Matematica Italiana (Dec 2025 per blog). A search snippet gives publication 7 Jan 2026, DOI 10.1007/s40574-025-00525-z; that Springer page redirected to a sign-in and was not read.

events.delivers: Nothing about ℵ_ω. It collects necessary conditions for successors of singulars in general, a neighbouring question.
events.remains: The whole ℵ_ω question, which the survey does not address in the arXiv text.

events.what_happened: Monroe Eskew and Masahiro Shioya, 'Chang's Conjectures and Easton collapses' (arXiv:2402.09917). A simplified construction, via Easton collapses, of a model where Chang's Conjecture for triples holds (main results at ω_1–ω_3). The introduction mentions a planned sequel on many instances of CC for triples below ω_ω. The page contains no Jónsson or ℵ_ω result.

events.direction: No bearing on the Jónsson question.

events.what_happened: Omer Ben-Neria and Shimon Garti, 'Jónsson and Magidor filters' (arXiv:2503.13744, submitted 17 Mar 2025). Filter versions of square-bracket partition relations under the Axiom of Determinacy: singular cardinals in a Kleinberg sequence above a strong partition cardinal are not Magidor, but the sequence's limit is; forcing over an AD model gives a singular cardinal carrying a Magidor filter. 'Jonssonicity' here names a filter property. The abstract does not name ℵ_ω and says nothing about Jónsson algebras.
events.delivers: A filter-partition result under AD. This is a choiceless setting, not ZFC, and it is not about existence of a Jónsson algebra.
events.direction: No bearing on Jónsson algebras on ℵ_ω. A different property under a hypothesis incompatible with ZFC.

events.what_happened: Shimon Garti, Yair Hayut and Saharon Shelah, 'On a problem of Erdős and Hajnal' (arXiv:2502.16625; v1 23 Feb 2025, v2 25 Jun 2026). Addresses the ordinary partition relation ℵ_{ω+1} ↛ (ℵ_{ω+1},(3)_{ℵ0})^2: consistent with λ a strong limit and 2^λ > λ^+, and 'can be pushed down to ℵ_ω'. The abstract does not mention Jónsson algebras or Jónsson cardinals.
events.revisions: v1 23 Feb 2025; v2 25 Jun 2026 (content not read).
events.delivers: A partition-relation consistency result at ℵ_{ω+1} and ℵ_ω. Not Jónsson.
events.direction: No bearing on the Jónsson question.

events.what_happened: Sungchul Lee, forum post on erdosproblems.com, thread 623 (4 Jun 2026, 13:39). Claims an independence result for Erdős Problem 623, which asks: X of cardinality ℵ_ω, f from finite subsets of X to X with f(A) not in A; must there be an infinite independent Y? The post says that in ZFC the positive assertion E623 is equivalent to Koepke's free-subset property Fr_ω(ℵ_ω, ω); that Con(ZFC+E623) is equivalent to Con(ZFC + a measurable cardinal); and that Con(ZFC+¬E623) is equivalent to Con(ZFC). Manuscript and LaTeX in a GitHub repository (github.com/lsngchl/Erdos1208, per search; not opened). The thread's replies are listed under 'checked_by'. The post says it was assisted by GPT-5.5 Pro. The teorth/erdosproblems AI-contributions wiki (opened) lists this under 1(d) (AI collaborating with humans) with status 'Candidate full solution', unverified.
events.revisions: Per the post (summary by fetch tool): a v2 of the manuscript replaced an appeal to Fremlin 543C with a direct elementary proof of the needed section inequality.
events.delivers: If correct: Erdős #623 is independent of ZFC, with the consistency strengths above. This is a claim about a free-subset property at ℵ_ω. It is a different question from the existence of a Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω. The sources read establish no link between Fr_ω(ℵ_ω, ω) and Jónsson algebras, and the Jónsson-free-subset link in Adolf and Ben-Neria (search snippet) is for regular cardinals only.
events.remains: The Jónsson question entirely. Erdős #623 is not a case of it.

summary: Searched 47 queries (listed below) and opened roughly two dozen arXiv, Wikipedia, erdosproblems and blog pages; several talk PDFs and the Springer page could not be read (see incomplete). Nothing found resolves whether a Jónsson algebra exists on ℵ_ω, in ZFC or relative to a hypothesis. The status in the sources is open. The ℵ_ω-specific results are all conditional. Eskew (2019/20) proves Silver's theorem and strengthenings, all assuming ℵ_ω is Jónsson, and says relative consistency is open. Dimonte (2016/17) shows ℵ_ω is Jónsson under a generic I0-type hypothesis in a choiceless setting. Ben-Neria and Lücke (first posted 14 Mar 2023; v2 18 Apr 2024; accepted at Canadian J. Math. in 2025 per snippet) prove that Jónssonness of ℵ_ω implies Σ1-stationarity of the sequence {ℵ_n} (Theorem 4.14) and an equiconsistency with a measurable for a different property (Theorem 5.3). Their Section 6 poses questions, none on existence. The only in-window item on this exact question is the April 2024 revision of that paper, and its first written argument predates the window; no changelog was shown, so I could not say what changed. Terminology: 'ℵ_ω is Jónsson' is the no-algebra answer, so Eskew, Dimonte and Ben-Neria–Lücke all sit on the 'no' side conditionally. Close calls: (a) Ben-Neria–Lücke moves what is known conditionally about ℵ_ω if it is Jónsson, not whether a Jónsson algebra exists, so I recorded it as conditional, not as movement of the quantity. (b) Erdős #623 (Lee, 4 Jun 2026, with 'GPT-5.5 Pro' assistance, claiming ZFC independence of a free-subset statement equivalent to Koepke's Fr_ω(ℵ_ω, ω)) is the one AI-involved ℵ_ω set-theory claim in the window. I judged it a different question: it asks about a function on finite subsets and independent sets, not about algebras and subalgebras, and no source connects the two. I recorded it and discounted it. (c) Shelah's 1978 ℵ_{ω+1} Jónsson algebra makes ℵ_ω the least open case, via the successor transfer; it does not decide ℵ_ω. AI search: I found no AI involvement in any source on Jónsson algebras or ℵ_ω. The sources read in full text or with an acknowledgements section (Eskew, Ben-Neria–Lücke, Rinot's arXiv text, Soukup–Szentmiklóssy's abstract page where its acknowledgements are not shown, Poveda–Thei, Eskew–Shioya) name no AI system. For Ben-Neria–Garti, Garti–Hayut–Shelah, Dimonte, Shelah 1998 and DuBeau I read only the abstract page, so their 'none found' is weaker. The AI-contributions wiki (teorth/erdosproblems, data to 30 Jun 2026) has no entry on Jónsson or set theory beyond Erdős #623 and an unrelated Shelah 1998 problem (#1036, formalised with Aristotle, 20 Jan 2026, subject not confirmed). Not recorded: a single Spanish-language secondary report (Oct 2026) of an OpenAI preprint on the Partition Principle not implying choice. It concerns a different problem, I could not find the preprint, and it bears on nothing here.
competing_reading: Read the Ben-Neria–Lücke line as real movement. Its 2024 revision and 2025 journal acceptance are the newest peer-reviewed items about ℵ_ω being Jónsson. They show Jónssonness of ℵ_ω has definable-club consequences, and their stated aim is to restrict the models of set theory in which ℵ_ω can be Jónsson. A reader who counts restriction of models as progress would record movement. The other reading is that no quantity named in the problem moved, since every ℵ_ω result is conditional on the no-algebra side. A reader could also treat Lee's Erdős #623 claim as evidence that ℵ_ω-level combinatorics is independent of ZFC, and so as a hint that the Jónsson question may be too. That is an analogy with no link established in the sources.
what_would_settle_it: A yes answer needs a ZFC construction of a Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω. A no answer needs a ZFC proof that ℵ_ω is Jónsson. Independence needs consistency results both ways: a model with a Jónsson algebra on ℵ_ω, and a model where ℵ_ω is Jónsson from large cardinals. The in-window checks that would move the record: (1) the published Canadian J. Math. version of Ben-Neria–Lücke, to read the Section 6 question list and check whether v2 changed Theorem 4.14; (2) a readable copy of the Lücke 'Σ1-definability at higher cardinals' talk (Vienna, 30 Jun 2025) and of the Eskew Münster slides, to see whether they state anything new; (3) the Erdős #623 manuscript, only to confirm it has no bearing on Jónsson algebras, which the abstract and forum thread suggest it does not.
